# Upstream tests skipped by the production-rules job of .github/workflows/socialhq-ci.yml.
# They assert TryPost's rules, which Social HQ replaces in production, so they
# fail there by design. One test per line, "<TestFile>::<test description>",
# optionally followed by " with data set "<dataset>"" (as Pest prints it) to skip
# only that dataset. bin/socialhq-production-rules-filter turns the list into
# the --exclude-filter pattern.
# Found by running the suites with the four rules on (2026-11-16 audit, M21).
# A test removed upstream can be dropped from here; one that starts failing in
# that job is a regression to look at, not a line to add without a reason.

# AcceptInviteControllerTest: an invite without a role joins with the built-in role its flags match (Social HQ roles, PATCHES row 301); with members always reviewed (SOCIALHQ_MEMBERS_ALWAYS_REVIEWED) TryPost's "member who publishes directly" is an Editor, whose stored flag says it needs approval. What the member may do is the same as before.
AcceptInviteControllerTest::accept invite assigns the exact access from the invite with data set "('member')"

# AccountLimitAndAccessParityTest: agents: an API key or MCP grant, admins' too, sends posts for approval and can neither approve nor manage repurposes (SOCIALHQ_AGENT_POSTS_REVIEWED); and members who are not admins always need approval and never approve (SOCIALHQ_MEMBERS_ALWAYS_REVIEWED): TryPost's "member who publishes directly" no longer exists.
AccountLimitAndAccessParityTest::the workspace owner is an admin who publishes directly through api and mcp
AccountLimitAndAccessParityTest::the workspace says what the caller may do through mcp with data set "dataset "member""

# ApiRouteSweepTest: agents: an API key or MCP grant, admins' too, sends posts for approval and can neither approve nor manage repurposes (SOCIALHQ_AGENT_POSTS_REVIEWED).
ApiRouteSweepTest::a malformed id inside a body is a validation error, never a database error
